sections.h2: Where is Morton County, North Dakota?
sections.html:
Morton County is in south-central North Dakota, with the Missouri River running along its east boundary and Mandan as its county seat and largest city. It covers about 1,945 square miles, making it the seventh largest county in the state by area.

The 2020 census counted 33,291 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 34,601. That ranks it sixth in population among the state's counties. Neighbors are Oliver, Burleigh, Emmons, Sioux, Grant, Stark and Mercer counties.

Morton County is part of the Bismarck metropolitan area. Burleigh County and the state capital of Bismarck lie across the river, and the county tax offices sit in Mandan.

sections.h2: What is the landscape like and how did the county form?
sections.html:
The terrain is low rolling hills cut by gullies and drainages, with level farmland in places. The Cannonball River runs along part of the south boundary, and Lake Oahe, Lake Patricia and the Lake Patricia National Wildlife Refuge are among the water features. The high point is 2,375 feet.

The Dakota Territory legislature created the county on January 8, 1873, and it was organized on November 5, 1878. A settlement appeared in 1878 after the Northern Pacific Railroad chose a western approach to its Missouri River bridge, and it later became Mandan. In 1916 land was split off to form Grant County, which fixed the current boundaries.

A 72-mile stretch of the Dakota Access Pipeline passes through the county.

sections.h2: What is Mandan like for homeowners and sellers?
sections.html:
Mandan is on I-94 just west of the Missouri River and across from Bismarck. The city's business development office describes the economy as diverse, naming oil, energy, agriculture, tourism, healthcare, government services, technology and manufacturing.

Interstate 94 and Highways 1806, 6 and 25 carry traffic through the city, and people from towns such as Hebron, New Salem, Flasher and Glen Ullin travel to or through Mandan for routine purchases. The Bismarck airport has daily Delta service to Minneapolis-St. Paul, United to Denver and American to Dallas-Fort Worth and Chicago. BNSF and the Dakota Missouri Valley Western Railroad provide freight rail.

  • I-94 corridor in north Mandan
  • East Mandan along Memorial Highway near the river
  • Main Street and downtown Mandan

These are the areas the city names for retail-ready and commercial development.

sections.h2: Who assesses property in Morton County?
sections.html:
Two offices value property here. The county Tax Equalization Office oversees assessments in unincorporated areas and in cities and townships that contract with the county, while the City of Mandan runs its own Assessing and Building Inspections departments inside city limits.

The county assesses residential and commercial property at market value as of February 1 each year, and farmland follows the state's agricultural valuation guide. The county is split into ten zones so each property is reassessed at least once every ten years. Owners in the current zone receive a letter offering an assessor appointment or a property detail sheet to complete.

Building permits follow the same split. The county Building Inspector handles unincorporated areas, plus Almont and Glen Ullin at those cities' request. Flasher, Hebron and New Salem issue their own.

sections.h2: What credits can lower a Morton County bill?
sections.html:
Morton County lists three programs that reduce residential tax, each tied to the owner's status.

  • Homestead Property Tax Credit: owners 65 or older or disabled whose household income does not exceed $70,000 after medical deductions
  • Disabled Veterans Property Tax Credit: veterans with a disability of 50 percent or more
  • Primary Residence Credit, administered by the State Tax Commissioner

The county also publishes a property tax calculator and a farm residence exemption page through the Tax Equalization Office.

sections.h2: Who is the Morton County Treasurer and when are taxes due?
sections.html:
The Morton County Treasurer's office is at 210 2nd Ave NW, Mandan, ND 58554, phone 701-667-3310, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. except holidays. The treasurer is elected to a four-year term and collects real estate and mobile home taxes.

The office mails statements and delinquent notices and gives lenders the figures they need for escrow accounts. Taxes are due January 1 and payable without penalty through March 1, and paying the full year by February 15 earns a 5 percent discount.

The penalty schedule in North Dakota Century Code section 57-20-01 adds 3 percent after March 1, then 3 percent on May 1, July 1 and October 15. The second installment takes 6 percent after October 15.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Morton County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the assessor right away and ask for a review, since many questions are settled without a hearing. Assessment letters carry each property's proposed true and full value.

If that does not resolve it, appeal at the local equalization meetings, which cover the current year's valuation. Cities and townships meet in April, the Morton County Board of Equalization meets in early June, and the State Board of Equalization completes its review in August. The state board can lower a value only if you appeared at both the local and county boards.

You can also file an abatement covering the current and previous years. The county's page puts the deadline at November 1 and says the applicant has the burden of proof, so confirm the year with the office. Forms are on the State Tax Commissioner's site or from the county.

sections.h2: What is the Morton County delinquent tax timeline?
sections.html:
A property becomes subject to tax lien foreclosure when taxes, specials and interest stay delinquent in the third year. The county auditor tracks these parcels, notifies interested parties and holds an annual sale.

WhenStep
Before June 1Foreclosure notice goes to the owner, occupants and others with an interest
Before August 1Notice of delinquent property published in the official county newspaper
October 1, 5 p.m.Everything owed must be paid to the County Treasurer
After October 1Owner can still pay in full before the sale starts
Third Tuesday of NovemberAnnual sale

Sale notices are posted at least 15 days before the sale in the auditor's office and on the county website, and published at least 10 days before in the county newspaper.

sections.h2: How does selling a Morton County house with tax due work?
sections.html:
You can sell and pay the tax from the proceeds, and a cash buyer can close faster than a lender-financed sale. The title company gets the payoff from the Treasurer and pays it at closing.

The delinquency calendar is the reason to act early. Once a county takes a tax deed, an owner can buy the property back only before resale, either in full or under an installment contract with at least 25 percent paid in cash, according to Nolo's summary of the statutes. A tax foreclosure can also wipe out a mortgage because the tax lien has priority.

We buy Morton County houses as they are, including homes in Mandan and in the smaller towns, and we work with your title company on the county payoff.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Morton County?
faqs.a: The Morton County Treasurer, at 210 2nd Ave NW in Mandan. The office phone is 701-667-3310.

faqs.q: Does Mandan assess its own property?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Mandan runs its own assessing and building inspection departments for properties inside city limits, while the county assesses unincorporated areas and contracting towns.

faqs.q: When is Morton County property tax due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due January 1 and payable without penalty until March 1. Paying in full by February 15 earns a 5 percent discount, and the second installment date is October 15.

faqs.q: What date does Morton County foreclose tax liens?
faqs.a: The tax lien foreclosure date is October 1 at 5 p.m. The county's annual sale of delinquent property falls on the third Tuesday of November.

faqs.q: Which credits can reduce a Morton County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Homestead Credit, the Disabled Veterans Credit and the Primary Residence Credit. The homestead income limit listed by the county is $70,000 after medical deductions.
